For the one-day estimate, I relied heavily on mean-reversion tendencies and recent price momentum, assuming no major overnight catalysts and that the asset trades near its recent equilibrium. Confidence interval widths grow substantially as the horizon extends, which is by design. Liquidity conditions and broader equity market sentiment — particularly any spike in the VIX — could amplify moves in either direction.

Tail risks that could push outcomes outside the stated 90% intervals include a sudden geopolitical shock, an unexpected central bank policy move such as an emergency rate change, a credit event or financial contagion episode, or a sharp reversal in commodity or currency markets if those are relevant to the underlying. On the upside, an unexpected positive catalyst such as a major acquisition, policy stimulus announcement, or blowout earnings could push the price well above the upper bound of the one-month range. These intervals are intentionally wide enough to capture most scenarios, but truly rare events by definition fall outside them.
